title: Vasquez: Catholic truth is that images are owed adoration-signs; iconomachs who withhold kiss and bow are heretics under Nicaea II
source_text: XXXIII. Ac proinde merito Vasquez asserit, juxta Scholae Romanae mentem, Catholicam veritatem esse, quod imaginibus deferenda sit adoratio, hoc est, signa servitutis & submissionis, amplexu, luminaribus, oblatione suffituum, capitis nudatione, &c. Adeoque non simpliciter errantibus, sed Iconomachis haereticis accenset eos, qui tempore septimae Synodi, judicarunt imagines ubique retinendas esse, non ad solum ornatum, sed etiam ad excitandam fidelibus memoriam exemplaris, ut coram eis ipsum venerarentur, imaginibus tamen nullum signum honoris, aut submissionis, neque osculo, nec inclinatione corporis, nec alio modo exhibebant, quia istud dicebant esse idololatriam. Quare nec osculabantur imagines, neque ipsis corpus inclinabant, nec thurificabant: sed recti coram eis, in memoriam exemplaris excitati, in ipsum mente sola ferebantur. Quo nomine fuerunt in Synodo septima damnati; & contra eos in illa Synodo definitum est, non sufficere si quis dicat imagines se venerari, nisi illas etiam adoret. * In 3. part. Tho. tom. 1. disputat. 106. cap. 1. & 2.
pass_a_gloss: And therefore Vasquez deservedly asserts, according to the mind of the Roman School, that it is Catholic truth that adoration is to be paid to images, that is, signs of servitude and submission—by embrace, lights, offering of incense, uncovering of the head, etc. And so he reckons those not simply as erring but as Iconomach heretics who in the time of the seventh Synod judged that images were to be kept everywhere, not for ornament alone but also to excite in the faithful the memory of the exemplar so that before them they might venerate it, yet exhibited to the images no sign of honor or submission, neither by kiss nor by inclination of the body nor in any other way, because they said that was idolatry. Wherefore they neither kissed images, nor inclined the body to them, nor offered incense: but standing upright before them, stirred to the memory of the exemplar, they were borne to it by the mind alone. On which account they were condemned in the seventh Synod; and against them it was defined in that Synod that it does not suffice if someone says he venerates images, unless he also adores them. * On 3rd part of Thomas, tom. 1, disput. 106, ch. 1 & 2.
pass_b_english: Vasquez: owed image-adoration (kiss, lights, incense, bare head) is Catholic truth.
Seventh-Synod ‘iconomachs’ who kept images for memory but refused bodily honor-signs were condemned—veneration without adoration is not enough.

choices.why: Council standard Vasquez enforces against mental-only honor.
